spec.requirements:
# Requirements: Migrate moment to dayjs

## Context

- Deprecated: "Webpack/react-app-scripts crash" (npm.version.deprecated)
- 3 known vulnerabilities in 2.19.0 (GHSA-446m-mv8f-q348, GHSA-8hfj-j24r-96c4, GHSA-wc69-rhjr-hc9g) (osv.querybatch.results[].vulns[].id)
- Successor: dayjs. moment is in maintenance mode; dayjs has a near-identical API in 2 kB (curated.successors[moment])
- Maintainers describe the project as legacy / maintenance-only (curated.legacy[moment])

Scope: 3 source files scanned, 2 need changes.

## User stories

- As a maintainer, I want to stop depending on `moment` so that I no longer ship an unmaintained dependency.
- As a reviewer, I want proof that behaviour is unchanged so that I can merge with confidence.

## Acceptance criteria (EARS)

- R1.1 WHEN the migration patch is applied THE SYSTEM SHALL contain no import or require of `moment` in the 2 migrated files.
- R1.2 WHEN `package.json` is read THE SYSTEM SHALL no longer list `moment` as a dependency, unless unmigrated usage remains.
- R2.1 WHEN the differential property-based tests run THE SYSTEM SHALL show identical observable behaviour between `moment` and dayjs for the covered operations over at least 100 generated inputs each.
- R2.2 IF a call site uses behaviour the recipe cannot express THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL leave a `TODO(revenant)` comment and list it in the migration notes instead of silently changing it.
- R3.1 WHERE the project's own test suite exists THE SYSTEM SHALL pass it unchanged after the migration.
spec.design:
# Design: Migrate moment to dayjs

## Approach

Apply the curated `moment-to-dayjs` recipe: a deterministic source transform, a `package.json` edit. Verification is differential: the old and new implementations run side by side under fast-check.

## Flow

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A[Scan: moment@2.19.0 flagged] --> B[Recipe moment-to-dayjs]
  B --> C[Patch: 2 files]
  B --> D[Differential PBT]
  C --> E{Tests green?}
  D --> E
  E -- yes --> F[Open PR]
  E -- no --> G[Review TODO notes]
```

## Known limits

- moment mutates in place, dayjs is immutable: mutating calls whose result is discarded are flagged with a TODO, not rewritten.
- moment-timezone, locales and custom parsing formats need manual review (flagged with TODOs).
- Differential tests cover format, add/subtract, startOf/endOf, diff, comparison and ISO parsing for pure date maths; they do not prove plugin behaviour such as relativeTime wording.

## Files changed

- `src/audit.js`
- `src/server.js`
